=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- File: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
  Line or code reference: 2666
  Problem: The completion-mark regex `[ x]` matches only lowercase `[x]`. The sibling regex `TRACKING_BODY_ISSUE_LINE_RE` at line 54 uses `[ xX]`, accepting both `[x]` and `[X]`. If a tracking issue body ever contains `[X]` (a manual operator edit, or future rendering), `parse_tracking_body` sets `completed=false`, so `rebuild_tracking_state` never triggers the `ReconstructionUnsafeError` guard and proceeds to re-create already-finished work as duplicates.
  Why it fails at runtime: An operator manually checks a sub-issue with `[X]`. After a transient API failure blanks the state comment, `parse_tracking_body` reads the body, sees `[X]`, classifies it as incomplete, and the unmapped-completed check finds nothing to refuse. `rebuild_tracking_state` resets `current_wave` to 1 and the already-merged issue is re-created as a duplicate  the exact failure mode the guard exists to prevent.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/orchestrate_lib.py
  Line or code reference: 2642-2647
  Problem: The `parse_tracking_body` docstring documents wave entries as `{id, title, priority}`. After this PR, every issue dict also carries a `completed` boolean key. The docstring is stale and misleads callers and future editors about the returned shape.
  Why it fails at runtime: No immediate runtime failure. `rebuild_tracking_state` is the only consumer of the new key today and handles it correctly. However, callers that introspect the documented contract will find an unexpected key, and future editors may remove or mishandle it based on the outdated docstring.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  Why it fails at runtime: When lookup encounters unexpected body shape, treats failure as success and proceeds to create duplicate issues.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
